title: System Binary Proxy Execution: Mshta
summary: Mshta.exe is the Windows utility that runs Microsoft HTML Applications, known as HTAs, which are standalone programs built from HTML, JavaScript or VBScript and executed through Internet Explorer components but outside the browser window. Because they run outside that browser context, the security zones, script restrictions and download prompts that would normally apply to web content do not constrain them, which makes an HTA an effective container for a payload or a downloader. An adversary exploits the utility's flexible input handling: it accepts a path to a local .hta file, a URL pointing at a remotely hosted HTA or COM scriptlet, or an inline script expression supplied directly on the command line, so execution can begin from a single short command with nothing written to disk first. Mshta is signed and native to Windows, so application control deployments that do not consider it may permit the activity. Detection centres on process creation for mshta.exe whose arguments contain a web address or an inline script prefix, image and child process relationships in which mshta spawns command shells, script hosts or PowerShell, network connections originating from mshta.exe, and temporary file writes that precede or follow it. Legitimate use is uncommon and typically involves a legacy line-of-business application opening a local HTA from a managed directory with no child process and no outbound connection.

beginner.definition: An HTML Application, or HTA, is a small program written with web languages such as HTML and script. Windows runs these programs with mshta.exe, a signed Microsoft tool. They run outside the browser, so browser safety settings do not apply to them.
beginner.whyItMatters: A single short command can make mshta.exe fetch a program from the internet and run it. Nothing needs to be saved on the disk first, which leaves less evidence. Because the tool is signed and native, allowlists may accept it. If you ignore this, a user clicking one link can start a full infection chain.
howItWorks: An HTML Application, or HTA, is a small program written in web languages such as HTML and script.
Windows runs it with mshta.exe, which uses the same engine as the old Internet Explorer browser.
The program runs outside the browser, so the browser's own safety settings do not apply to it.
mshta.exe accepts a web address as an argument, so the program does not need to be saved first.
It also accepts script typed straight into the command line, which keeps the whole thing to one command.
The script then downloads a larger program and starts it, which is where the main payload arrives.
beginner.example: A street food van has a permit to park on the town square, so the warden never stops it. The menu board on the side is only a sign, and the warden only checks the permit. Behind the counter, staff are quietly carrying goods into the shop next door. Nobody looks inside the van, because the permit is valid. mshta.exe is the van, and the Microsoft signature is the permit.
takeaways: HTA files run outside the browser, so browser protections do not cover them.
A command line that starts with mshta and contains a web address is a strong warning sign.
Watch for mshta.exe starting other programs or making network connections.

objectives: Explain what an HTA file is and which Windows utility executes it.
Describe three input forms mshta.exe accepts and what each one enables.
Explain how this sub-technique differs from the System Binary Proxy Execution parent technique.
Explain why HTA content is not governed by browser security settings.
Identify the command line, child process and network evidence that indicates mshta abuse.
